# Why does queue overflow and underflow cause burst oscillations when bridging 50 Hz remote operation to 250 Hz execution layer?

> **Current answer:** Average frequency equality does not imply strict synchronization of instantaneous production and consumption. Python scheduling, ROS transmission, and batch write-inflated data cause bursts; if the queue is full and new targets are discarded, the execution layer continues to consume old trajectories, leading to increasing delays and target jumps upon recovery. Double-ended monotonic clocks and queue watermarks should be recorded, and bounded buffers, expired command discarding, and target continuity protection should be set.

## Key terms

- Producer-consumer (producer-consumer) (生产者—消费者)
- Queue depth (queue depth) (队列水位)
- Latency jitter (latency jitter) (时延抖动)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to stably send 50 Hz upper-level commands to the 250 Hz lower-level execution loop?
- Why does queue overflow and queue underflow both manifest as robot jitter?
- Queue overflow discards new messages, leading to long delays and sudden large oscillations.
- Delay decreases after discarding 1/5 of the messages, but the queue is exhausted and continues to jitter.

## Environment

- Upper-level remote operation at 50 Hz/20 ms; lower-level C++ execution at 250 Hz/4 ms; ROS topic; maximum queue of 5000, cumulative 10 messages after execution.

## Priority diagnostics

- Record the upper-level production timestamp, lower-level consumption timestamp, queue depth, packet loss count, and target continuity.

## Possible causes

- Inconsistent time/scheduling between Python and C++ endpoints.
- Fixed five-part interpolation does not handle network jitter and production-consumption offset.

## Attempts

- Divide each 20 ms command into 5 parts for 4 ms execution by the execution layer.
- Discard 1/5 of the messages to reduce queue growth.
- Plan to switch the Python middle layer to C++.

## Result

- First solution still causes queue overflow; second solution reduces delay but causes underload jitter; final C++ rewrite direction is not publicly verified.

## Limitations

- Raises questions about the factual basis of the total bus; no public timestamp curve, packet loss rate, or final rewrite result is provided.

## Safety notes

- Limit joint speed, position increments, and torque during real machine testing; maintain the last safe target or enter damping mode when queue is abnormal; do not directly convert missing frames into abrupt jumps.
